entry.title: Everything But The Girl Announce New Album Blue Reservoir: Hear “Young And Dumb”
entry.summary: They got me with this one. Everything But The Girl, the long-running UK duo of married couple Tracey Thorn and Ben Watt, recently started releasing new music and playing live again after a decades-long break, and the first single from their upcoming album Blue Reservoir is all about aging and missing the version of yourself…
entry.content:
They got me with this one. Everything But The Girl, the long-running UK duo of married couple Tracey Thorn and Ben Watt, recently started releasing new music and playing live again after a decades-long break, and the first single from their upcoming album Blue Reservoir is all about aging and missing the version of yourself that did ridiculous, passionate, self-destructive things all the time. In a soft and husky rasp, Thorn sings, "Yes I’m older and wiser/ I know more than I did then/ But I’d give up all the wisdom to be young and dumb again." Whoof. That's too real. I'm not sure I was ready to confront that level of realness on a Wednesday morning in October.

Everything But The Girl started way back in 1982, and they went through a number of different styles, from the slinky sophisti-pop of their early days to the slinky drum 'n' bass that they adapted in the late '90s. (The sounds were different, but the slinkiness remained.) EBTG went inactive after 1999's Temperamental — great album — so that Thorn and Watt could focus on their solo careers. In 2023, they returned with the comeback album Fuse, which found them playing around with dance textures once again. Last year, they returned to performing live after a quarter century, playing a series of sold-out shows at the MOTH Club, a small London venue. Today, they announce Blue Reservoir, a new album directly inspired by their MOTH Club experience.

In a press release, Tracey Thorn talks about how much the duo enjoyed the experience of those MOTH Club shows: "There was an intensity and simplicity to the MOTH shows that took us back to how we started out. Direct, rooted in guitar and voice, a few extra colors. We hadn’t been in that world for a long time, and it just felt fresh and real."

In response, Ben Watt bought a Spanish nylon-string guitar, and the duo went back to writing the kind of lush, thoughtful songs that they made when they were starting out. Watt says, "It is the sound of so much of the music I first connected with growing up, and I’d never actually owned one. It became quite an emotional springboard for me. I found a voice I thought I’d lost."

"Young And Dumb," for instance, is a soft acoustic song with a lilting bossa nova rhythm. It's one of the songs that Everything But The Girl wrote earlier this year, drawing on Latin music and English folk. They recorded most of the album live at London's RAK Studios, with a band that included double bassist Rex Horan, drummer Evan Jenkins, and percussionist Fabio de Oliveira, those father Bosco was a big influence on Everything But The Girl's 1984 debut Eden. Thorn and Watt's son Blake Watt, now of the London indie-folk band Family Stereo, guests on two songs, and Ben Watt overdubbed in some extra stuff at home later.

Tracey Thorn and Ben Watt wrote the treatment for the "Young And Dumb" video, and Edward Bishop directed it, shooting it at the MOTH Club. It's a single-shot performance with a few surprises, and it really lets you focus on the song, which got under my skin immediately. Thorn and Watt are both in their sixties, and I find the song to be a beautiful way of reckoning with the passage of time. Check it out below.

entry.title: My Chemical Romance Bow To Pressure From Dallas Cowboys Cheerleaders
entry.summary: My Chemical Romance are out on the road performing their 2006 classic The Black Parade for its 20th anniversary. As is the band’s custom, the live show involves a great deal of pageantry, including a staged shootout involving fake Dallas Cowboys Cheerleaders that took place at the Hollywood Bowl last Wednesday, then again on Thursday.…
entry.content:
My Chemical Romance are out on the road performing their 2006 classic The Black Parade for its 20th anniversary. As is the band's custom, the live show involves a great deal of pageantry, including a staged shootout involving fake Dallas Cowboys Cheerleaders that took place at the Hollywood Bowl last Wednesday, then again on Thursday.

The real Dallas Cowboys Cheerleaders got wind of this and filed a temporary restraining order and injunction against MCR, arguing that the performance might lead the public to believe the cheerleaders had signed off on this. Specifically, the cheerleaders' parent company Pro Silver Star Ltd. filed the lawsuit. In their complaint, Pro Silver Star alleged that the band ignored a cease-and-desist issued Thursday. They have not, however, ignored the legal action.

My Chemical Romance have agreed to stop using Dallas Cowboys Cheerleader lookalike uniforms in their live shows, TMZ reports. It's a somewhat surprising decision coming after legal experts told Billboard the DCC parody was likely protected under the First Amendment, but maybe Gerard Way did not want to go to court over this matter.

In other Dallas Cowboys Cheerleaders news, they successfully unionized!

entry.content:
Meiv is the genre-hopping, geography-spanning project of Tokyo-based artist Curinus, his Hong Kong-based musical partner Eugene Nx, and the latter's young daughter Sara Nx. After introducing themselves last month with the kaleidoscopic debut single "Dedeoka," which was produced by American electronic artist Body Meat, they're back with another track.

True to its name, the song unfolds in two distinct chapters, kicking off with nonsensically sing-song lyrics and colorful organ blurts before vibe-shifting into something decidedly more downbeat. entry.title: Stephen Steinbrink – “I’m A Swimming Pool”
entry.summary: Oakland singer-songwriter and visual artist Stephen Steinbrink is releasing his new album In A Split Mirror at the end of the week
entry.content:
Oakland singer-songwriter and visual artist Stephen Steinbrink is releasing his new album In A Split Mirror at the end of the week. We've already heard its meditative lead single "Magic Mirror." Today, he's sharing one last single before the full release, the gently rippling "I'm A Swimming Pool," which comes with a colorful animated music video made by Steinbrink himself. As he explains:

When I was a kid in Arizona, I would swim in my friend’s pool. My favorite move was to hold my breath, float face down and try to create as little rippling in the water as possible to achieve this feeling of total weightlessness. In Phoenix summers, the upper depths of the water wasn’t too far off from matching my internal temperature and it created this sensation of disconnection from my body that I loved, feeling like I was a part of the water. It's about being in the pool.

I made the accompanying animation by collaging together photographs I've taken over the years with other external images to create little phantasmagorical tableaus. I drew them over several months, drawing the same image over and over again and then animating them together to create the breathing, boiling movement in the colors and textures.

Listen below.

In A Split Mirror is out 10/30 on Sedimentary Archive/Mansions And Millions. Pre-order it here.

entry.title: St. Vincent Plays Fallon With Marc Ribot, Hannah Cohen, & Ella Hunt
entry.summary: Way back in 2017, St. Vincent ended her Jack Antonoff-produced album MASSEDUCTION with the arch, swirling ballad “Smoking Section.” She released a very different version of that song a couple of years later when Jlin remixed it. On Monday night, by way of promoting her recent in-concert album Live In London, St. Vincent got some…
entry.content:
Way back in 2017, St. Vincent ended her Jack Antonoff-produced album MASSEDUCTION with the arch, swirling ballad "Smoking Section." She released a very different version of that song a couple of years later when Jlin remixed it. On Monday night, by way of promoting her recent in-concert album Live In London, St. Vincent got some friends together to play "Smoking Section" on Jimmy Fallon's Tonight Show.

For last night's performance, Annie Clark sat at a table on a stage made up to look like a smoky hotel bar. She sang and played a lap steel that was up on the table next to her martini. Clark's regular keyboardist Rachel Eckroth played piano, but the rest of the band was full of ringers. Two backup singers sat next to Clark at that table: the spectral pop artist Hannah Cohen and the Scottish singer and actor Ella Hunt. Clark also had two stand-up bassists, James Genus from the Saturday Night Live band and Charlotte Kemp Muhl from the Ghost Of A Saber Tooth Tiger. And sitting on a nearby amp, she had downtown legend Marc Ribot — Clark's "favorite guitar player," as she writes on Instagram.

This was an extremely cool performance! It started off as a hazy torch song, and it built into something big and fiery without Clark ever having to stand up from her table. Ribot did some incredibly evocative shredding in there. The entire thing had serious Twin Peaks Roadhouse vibes, which cannot be easy to conjure when Jimmy Fallon is perched nearby. I strongly suggest that you watch it below.

Live In London is out now on Total Pleasure/BBC Studios.

entry.title: Taylor Swift Becomes Youngest Person Inducted Into Nashville Songwriters Hall Of Fame
entry.summary: Taylor Swift became the youngest woman inducted into the Songwriters Hall Of Fame in June. And as of now, the 36-year-old is also the youngest person in the Nashville Songwriters Hall Of Fame, which she officially entered alongside Lyle Lovett, Shawn Camp, Lee Thomas Miller, Bruce Channel, and the late Crickets drummer Jerry "J.I." Allison.
entry.content:
Taylor Swift became the youngest woman inducted into the Songwriters Hall Of Fame in June. And as of now, the 36-year-old is also the youngest person in the Nashville Songwriters Hall Of Fame, which she officially entered alongside Lyle Lovett, Shawn Camp, Lee Thomas Miller, Bruce Channel, and the late Crickets drummer Jerry "J.I." Allison.

In a star-studded gala at Nashville's Music City Center on Monday, Swift was inducted by her former tourmate Brad Paisley and honored with a bluegrass cover of her iconic Fearless hit "Love Story" performed by country star Lainey Wilson. Earlier this year, Swift was a surprise guest during Wilson's performance at Travis Kelce's Tight End University in Nashville.

After recalling the time that Paisley once filled her tour bus with live crickets in a prank-gone-too-far back in 2007, Swift began reminiscing about her early days in Nashville pursuing country stardom as a teenager.

"I was lucky enough to get a publishing deal with Sony Publishing when I was 14, and I just hit the ground running. I was like a sponge, and I had really curly hair and it was yellow, so I kind of looked like a sponge, too," Swift joked.

"I think you truly learn a craft when you do it over and over and over and that is what the magnificent songwriters that work in this amazing town do. There is no music community like this music community. I know. I checked all the communities," she added. "And I'm so incredibly honored to be inducted into this sacred club."

In other Taylor Swift news, Variety reports that leftist Brazilian president Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva's electoral victory over right-wing opponent Flavio Bolsonaro this week was aided significantly by support from Brazilian stan communities — particularly Swifties.

Brazilian Swifties shared memes of Lula in Swift music videos, Swift wearing Lula's hat, and more, with the hashtag #SwiftiesComLula (Swifties with Lula) trending on social media. "We’re inspired by these artists, and Taylor is always talking about how young people should take the lead," Josiane, a young Swiftie in São Paulo, told The Guardian last week.

Lula himself thanked the young people mobilizing to support him at a rally on São Paulo's Avenida Paulista last month. "I'm not sure whether to open this speech with 'comrades' or 'fandoms from all over Brazil,'" he joked.

entry.content:
From 2007 to 2015, Eric Harm was a member of Titus Andronicus on drums, percussion, and backing vocals. He returned to the band last year, and now he's announcing his debut solo album called All The Wrong Moves, produced by his bandmate Patrick Stickles.

"The character on All The Wrong Moves is the petty tyrant of the most pathetic kingdom," Harm explains, a sentiment which is evident from today's lead single "When You Move Back In." It begins with the charmingly self-deprecating hook: "I am a last-minute plan/ Card-carrying idiot."

"Patrick and I were glad to be back in each other's lives,” Harm says of Strickles' help on the LP. "After I had brought my voice to some Titus records where I could, he in turn had the right instincts to help with All The Wrong Moves." Titus bassist R.J. Gordon also did the engineering and mixing. Check out "When You Move Back In" below.

entry.title: EMA – “Total Control” (The Motels Cover)
entry.summary: I was just talking about how badly I missed getting new music from EMA. Past Life Martyred Saints, the solo debut from former Gowns leader Erika M. Anderson, is still one of my favorite albums of this century, and the two that followed were great, too. Right now, we’re coming up on a decade since…
entry.content:
I was just talking about how badly I missed getting new music from EMA. Past Life Martyred Saints, the solo debut from former Gowns leader Erika M. Anderson, is still one of my favorite albums of this century, and the two that followed were great, too. Right now, we're coming up on a decade since the release of Exile In The Outer Ring, the most recent EMA album. So it's extremely cool to see her randomly showing up again with a Motels cover that she recorded for an art piece.

I'm pretty sure the last thing that Erika M. Anderson released under the EMA name was a Modest Mouse cover from a 2021 Under The Radar compilation. In 2023, she started a supergroup called Thrash Palace with Talk Normal's Sarah Register and XBXRX's Vice Cooler, and they released a very cool two-song single on Sub Pop but then nothing else. Now, here she comes with her take on Berkeley new wave originators the Motels' 1979 single "Total Control."

Even in its original form, "Total Control" was a satirical six-minute epic about how you might sell your soul for total control over someone else. Tina Turner covered the song on the 1985 We Are The World album. EMA's version is part of "Memory As A Rock Out Of Reach," which she describes as "a hybrid media performance by EMA and artist Tabitha Nikolai." Here's a little more info, per the Bandcamp description:

Part origin story, part healing spell. "Memory As A Rock Out Of Reach" is a feature-length duet performance in which Erika M. Anderson (EMA) and visual artist Tabitha Nikolai use video game technologies to build out the psycho-sexual inner world of a girl-child in the '80s. Soundtracked by modular synth and guitar, a narrator searches for her shape amid commercial detritus, degraded 3D scans and a Polly Pocket apocalypse.

Cool! EMA's seven-minute take is pretty faithful to the original, but she reworks those prim new wave hooks by throwing them into heavy, sprawling space-rock overdrive. It sounds sick as hell. Below, check out EMA's "Total Control" cover and the Motels' original.

You can find more info on "Memory As A Rock Out Of Reach" here. It'll screen 11/21 at Portland's Tomorrow theater, with both EMA and Tabitha Nikolai in attendance.

entry.content:
Factory Floor are back. The UK electronic group began as a trio but were a duo by their second album, 2016's 25 25. Now they're a trio again and announcing the long-awaited followup One Trip, arriving just next month.

Original members Gabe Gurnsey and Nik Colk Void are joined by Joe Ward on additional percussion. Since last year, they've been releasing a string of singles: "Between You," "Tell Me," and "Buzz Saw." Today, there's two more singles: "Continuation" and "One Trip."

Their reunion began in 2024, when Factory Floor were invited to perform at Montreal's MUTEK. "After the MUTEK performance, we felt an appetite to work in a space where artists could connect emotionally and physically, both in the studio and on a live stage," the band says. "These environments hold more than sound; they carry a visceral energy that comes from being together. It's something we'd really missed as solo artists, and it made us want to explore that kind of experience again."

entry.content:
Back in the '90s, the Champaign, Illinois space-rockers Hum essentially invented the sound of American heavy shoegaze. Their records remain massively influential, especially with the current shoegaze revival still going strong. Hum broke up in 2000 but reunited a few times over the years. In 2020, they released the truly excellent comeback album Inlet. In 2021, drummer Bryan St. Pere passed away at the age of 51, and all band activities ceased. Earlier this year, however, Hum once again reassembled to headline Nothing's Slide Away festivals, where they played Inlet songs live for the first time, with Shiner's Jason Gerken on drums. Those sets got rapturous receptions, and now Hum are heading back out on tour.

Next year, Hum will hit the road on a series of short runs. Kansas City indie rock veterans the Life And Times will open all their shows, with Pelican and Spotlights also jumping on board for some of them. Jason Gerken actually filled in for the late Bryan St. Pere on Hum's last tour, way back in 2015, and he'll be back on drums again. You should expect this tour to be a big deal. entry.title: Karly Hartzman Debuts New Song And Covers Neil Young At Roy Cooper Rally
entry.summary: We’re one week away from the midterm election that will hopefully turn the Senate toward the Democrats and break the Trump administration’s hold on all three governmental branches. Down in North Carolina, the Democratic Senate candidate is former governor Roy Cooper, who is vying to replace the retiring Republican Senator Thom Tillis. Right now, Cooper…
entry.content:
We're one week away from the midterm election that will hopefully turn the Senate toward the Democrats and break the Trump administration's hold on all three governmental branches. Down in North Carolina, the Democratic Senate candidate is former governor Roy Cooper, who is vying to replace the retiring Republican Senator Thom Tillis. Right now, Cooper holds a very impressive polling lead, but the election hasn't happened yet. On Friday, a bunch of North Carolina musicians played a get-out-the-vote event for Cooper, and Wednesday leader Karly Hartzman was one of them.

On Friday night, Hartzman played a solo set at the Cat's Cradle in Carrboro, at an event that also included Hiss Golden Messenger, Tift Merritt, Watchhouse and Viv & Riley, and Davie Circle, and along with Governor Josh Stein and Justice Anita Earls — possibly the only time those acts have all shared the same bill. Hartzman's five-song set included thre Wednesday tracks, as well as another unidentified number that seems to be entirely new. Maybe that'll eventually be a Wednesday song, too.

Hartzman's set included a cover, too. She said that she'd tried to "conceive the most patriotic American thing I could possibly think of, who is a Canadian named Neil Young." She then covered "Barstool Blues," from Young's 1975 album Zuma. As it happens, Young is also in the news for campaign-related reasons today. Watch Hartzman play those songs below.

Nine Perfect Lives consists of Stella Wave and Helena Straight, and their haunting debut single “Die” is out today on AD 93. “I started writing ‘Die’ when I was living in LA…
entry.content:
Two members of Brooklyn indie rock trio Hello Mary launched a side-project together last year, and now their first release is finally here. Nine Perfect Lives consists of Stella Wave and Helena Straight, and their haunting debut single "Die" is out today on AD 93.

"I started writing 'Die' when I was living in LA and Stella was still in Brooklyn," Straight explains. "We made deliberate efforts to stay in touch and work on music but I wasn't yet sure when or if I was moving back to New York. I wrote and recorded a demo of the song in a few hours and realized that it was a direct response to Stella's heartbreak and confusion about my impulsive move across the country. Fleshing out the demo together felt effortless and reinforced our creative bond which was compromised in the context of Hello Mary at that time. 'Die' became the first NPL song so we are pleased for it to be our first single."

"Die" comes with a music video directed by Milo Hume. They also have some tour dates coming up opening for Friko and Lime Garden. Check out the video and dates below.

entry.title: Donnie Iris Of The Jaggerz & Wild Cherry Dead At 83
entry.summary: Donnie Iris, the Pittsburgh musician known for his time in the bands the Jaggerz and Wild Cherry, has passed away. The Pittsburgh Post-Gazette reports that Iris passed away on Monday after battling bladder cancer for years. Iris was 83. Donnie Iris was born Dominic Ierace, and he grew up in the suburbs of Pittsburgh. His…
entry.content:
Donnie Iris, the Pittsburgh musician known for his time in the bands the Jaggerz and Wild Cherry, has passed away. The Pittsburgh Post-Gazette reports that Iris passed away on Monday after battling bladder cancer for years. Iris was 83.

Donnie Iris was born Dominic Ierace, and he grew up in the suburbs of Pittsburgh. His mother had been a big-band singer, and he sang at weddings and entered talent contests as a kid. He fell in love with rock 'n' roll, taught himself guitar and drums, and formed a high-school doo-wop group called the Fabutons. He also formed and led a couple of bands while studying at Slippery Rock State College. In the mid-'60s, he formed the Jaggerz, who started off as a regional cover band before starting to write their own songs and releasing the 1969 debut album Introducing The Jaggerz. Their Iris-written song "The Rapper," a kind of bubblegum folk-rock jam that goes way harder than it has to, became a #2 pop hit in 1970.

The Jaggerz had a couple of minor hits after "The Rapper," but the band broke up after the commercial failure of their third album, 1975's Come Again. (The Jaggerz later reunited, but without Donnie Iris.) After the Jaggerz broke up, Iris joined Wild Cherry, the Ohio band who were riding high on the success of their 1976 smash "Play That Funky Music," as a guitarist and backup singer. Iris wasn't involved with "Play That Funky Music," though. Instead, he played on and helped engineer Wild Cherry's third album, 1978's I Love My Music. It was not a success, and Wild Cherry broke up in 1978.

Iris formed a new band, Donnie Iris And The Cruisers, with former Wild Cherry keyboardist Mark Avsec. They released their debut album Back On The Streets in 1980, and they scored a #29 hit with "Ah! Leah!," a gleaming example of that era's hard-charging studio-rock. Great song. A year later, they released their follow-up album King Cool, reaching the top 40 with "Love Is Like A Rock" and "My Girl." The Cruisers' later records didn't do as well, and a copyright lawsuit over "Ah! Leah!" further stalled their momentum. But Iris continued to crank out independent records and to perform for big crowds in the Pittsburgh area. He just played his final show last month before announcing his retirement for health reasons a couple of weeks later. Check out some of his work below.

entry.content:
Indietronica has never been so in. We've got ear, Lockimara, RIP Magic, to name a few emerging acts. There's also the Healing Power Of Horses, a UK duo who released their debut EP Summer Indoors (or outside wearing black) earlier this year. Now, they're already announcing their second EP of the year, 8725.

Like the aforementioned acts, the Healing Power Of Horses make off-kilter earworms that weave electronic elements into indie rock. To match the music, they maintain a cryptic aura. The two members are known as t and c, and here's what they offer about 8725:

Number 8725 is "Ithpeal" or "Imperfect" in the Brown-Driver-Briggs Hebrew & English Bible Lexicon and it is also the amount of songs we have left on a Samsung T5 1GB Portable SSD. This time we spent summer outdoors, but not in the way you think. Time is so short, Autumn has drawn in and we're beside ourselves with laughter. These songs are an angel gift to you the listener. Won't someone buy us a Tiffany lamp?

entry.summary: Last year, MJ Lenderman saluted a fellow indie singer-songwriter with an absolutely sick cover of This Is Lorelei’s “Dancing In The Club.” Lenderman’s version came out on a deluxe edition of This Is Lorelei’s Box for Buddy, Box For Star, and it stands as one of 2025’s best songs. Now, Lenderman has done something similar…
entry.content:
Last year, MJ Lenderman saluted a fellow indie singer-songwriter with an absolutely sick cover of This Is Lorelei's "Dancing In The Club." Lenderman's version came out on a deluxe edition of This Is Lorelei's Box for Buddy, Box For Star, and it stands as one of 2025's best songs. Now, Lenderman has done something similar for an indie songwriter from a completely different generation: Veteran Lambchop mastermind Kurt Wagner.

Earlier this year, Lambchop released the excellent album Punching The Clown. Today, Wagner announces a new EP called Demoed, which includes a bunch of different singers recording new vocals over the original Punching The Clown demo tracks. Fog's Andrew Broder, a longtime Lambchop collaborator, produced those demos. Besides Lenderman, the new singers are Alan Sparhawk, Circuit Des Yeux, Channy Leaneagh, Dan Wriggins, Lauren Auder, Flock Of Dimes, and more eaze.

The idea, as Kurt Wagner explains, is that he doesn't think his own presence is necessary for these songs to stand. Here's how he puts it:

I never knew what Herman Melville looked like until I was in high school. I just saw a picture in lit class and that was about it, nice beard. Prior to that, what Herman looked like was really not essential to my understanding or enjoyment of Moby Dick. It was distracting at best. I thought the work was the important thing. I mean, I still don’t know what Renoir looked like, but I bet he had a great beard. Great painter.

I used to fantasize that Lambchop would continue as an idea well beyond my participation. Over time, we’ve had at least two generations represented. A third now is beginning. And this is important to me, having the unique perspective and contributions from younger artists steering in the work we make. So i thought it would be nice, someday, that I might even step aside to watch and advise from the wings. Having a beard was never considered, but here we are.

This is to say that my idea of moving forward — aging with dignity — involves my disappearing from the notion of being the “dude,” the ego, entity, personality, figurehead, selfie guy, brand image. Who I am physically and how I appear becomes irrelevant. Allowing the concept and work to be the focus. My participation isn’t really necessary in the final presentation. Songwriting, “the song” implicitly allows for such a thing, or at least it did before pop culture insisted that it be part of the package. I mean, I get it, why that is and the way things are, but I've always felt it doesn’t have to be so, and there’s centuries of precedents to back this up.

Exhibit D: Andrew came up with the idea for a supplement to the new record. To ask artists we admired as both people and with unique voices to sing along to the initial guitar demos replacing me, thereby putting emphasis on their voices and the songs rather than my persona’s participation. A remix but backwards. Let’s admit it: Neil Sedaka was kinda goofy, but he sure could write a tune. I’m no Neil Sedaka, but I sure can be goofy.

We made a list of people to ask and sent them the demos along with the finished Punching The Clown album. We asked them to keep it simple and not overthink it, to keep it in the spirit of what a demo might be. Like a sketch for a painting, a demo. Sometimes they added other elements furthering their artistic involvement. It was their choice, their reaction to the premise and the tune.

Looking at it now, it does seem like one of those tribute records that happen after an artist dies or needs to raise funds for an operation or medical treatment. But I assure you, I am very much alive and all over what you hear here. Unlike cover versions of our songs, these are songs we made — I’m just not the singer. Jake, Haley, Alan, Channy, Dan, Lauren, Jenn, and Mari are.

For his part, MJ Lenderman has contributed a stripped-down, vulnerable version of "Weakened," the lush lead single from Punching The Clown. Below, check out Lenderman's take, the Lambchop original, and the Demoed tracklist.

TRACKLIST:
01 "Weakened (MJ Lenderman version)"
02 "A Doctor In The House (Circuit des Yeux / Alan Sparhawk version)"
03 "Stella (Channy Leaneagh version)"
04 "White People (Dan Wriggins version)"
05 "The New World Wave (Lauren Auder version)"
06 "Afterburner (Flock of Dimes version)"
07 "Andrew Jackson Asshat (More Eaze version)"

The Demoed EP is out 11/5 digitally and 2/5 physically on Merge.

entry.summary: Don’t get confused: There is a 1987 film called Wings Of Desire, a British indie rock duo named Wings Of Desire, and now a Mia Joy single titled “Wings Of Desire.” The song is what we’re talking about today, as it’s the dreamy lead single of her just-announced sophomore album Star Echo Heavy Dove. Star…
entry.content:
Don't get confused: There is a 1987 film called Wings Of Desire, a British indie rock duo named Wings Of Desire, and now a Mia Joy single titled "Wings Of Desire." The song is what we're talking about today, as it's the dreamy lead single of her just-announced sophomore album Star Echo Heavy Dove.

Star Echo Heavy Dove is the long-awaited followup to her sprawling 2021 debut, Spirit Tamer. The Chicago musician returned with "Comet" last month, which features Peel Dream Magazine. That track isn't on the record, but there is one guest on the LP: Midwife, whose brand of spacey ambient is completely compatible with Joy's entrancing sound.

"Wings Of Desire" is inspired by the movie of the same title, and here's what Joy says about:

Seeing Wenders' film for the first time helped me move internal static to words — one of those seminal moments in life where what you're watching mirrors life so dearly my only way to resolve myself was to write this song. I'm gravitated to lonely characters, solitude, longing. One of Star Echo Heavy Dove's motifs is centered around balancing the tug of war between feeling satisfaction with being self-sufficient and the willingness to give that up for the vulnerability of expanding desire. There's a great message in there about living for all that life offers, letting yourself go even if you end up bleeding. 

Dive into the mesmeric tune below.

TRACKLIST:
01 "Star Echo / Heavy Dove"
02 "4th Of July"
03 "Midnight"
04 "Wings Of Desire"
05 "Yes You Can"
06 "Easier"
07 "Circle" (Feat. Midwife)
08 "Patience"
09 "West"
10 "Saturn II"

Star Echo Heavy Dove is out 1/15/27 on Fire Talk. Pre-order it here.

entry.title: Macklemore Kicks Off Free Palestine Tour With Hozier, Kneecap, & Ed Sheeran’s Backing Band
entry.summary: Last month, Ed Sheeran dropped Macklemore as the opener of his US stadium tour — reportedly because of pressure from Patriots owner Robert Kraft, who doesn’t approve of Macklemore’s stance against Israel’s genocide of Palestinian people. Naturally, the resulted in a huge and justified backlash against Sheeran. All of Sheeran’s other openers quit the tour,…
entry.content:
Last month, Ed Sheeran dropped Macklemore as the opener of his US stadium tour — reportedly because of pressure from Patriots owner Robert Kraft, who doesn't approve of Macklemore's stance against Israel's genocide of Palestinian people. Naturally, the resulted in a huge and justified backlash against Sheeran. All of Sheeran's other openers quit the tour, as did Beoga, the Irish folk band who backed him up during part of his show. Sheeran claimed that he's "not complicit" and then made a tearful but meaningless speech once his tour resumed. Meanwhile, Sheeran's shows at Kraft's Gillette Stadium were canceled for severe weather anyway, and then Zach Bryan wore a "Free Palestine" shirt while playing the same stadium. In the meantime, Macklemore announced his Free Palestine benefit tour, and he kicked it off with some surprise guests Monday night in Dublin.

Macklemore already announced that he's donating the $1 million that he earned as an Ed Sheeran opener to Palestinian aid, then said that all the protests from his Free Palestine tour will support the same cause. He assembled the tour quickly, only announcing three shows at the beginning but promising more to come. The first of those shows was last night at Dublin's sold-out 3Arena. The evening was billed as "Macklemore and Friends," and none of the friends were announced ahead of time. When it went down last night, Macklemore's guests included the Irish pop-folk star Hozier, the staunchly pro-Palestine Dublin rap group Kneecap, and the former Ed Sheeran backing band Beoga.

Billboard reports that other guests included dead prez member M1, singer-songwriter Lina Makoul, and DJ Habibeats, as well as appearances from regular Macklemore collaborators like Australian singer Tones & I and "Same Love" guest Mary Lambert. Game Of Thrones star Liam Cunningham and activists Nadia Greenspan and Samir Eskand spoke to the crowd, and the show had remote appearances from the Strokes' Julian Casablancas, Mark Ruffalo, Cynthia Nixon, Ilana Glazer, and Natasha Rothwell.

A member of Beoga told the crowd, "You don't fuck with the Irish" and that "the tide is changing."

Hozier's set included a performance of the Irish folk ballad "The Prayer Of Shields," which Hozier reportedly learned from Lankum's Ian Lynch, and a screen behind him showed a QR code that took people to a petition for Ireland to expedite the process for 55 Palestinian students whose scholarships have been approved but who are still awaiting visas from the Irish government.

Kneecap's set naturally included a whole lot of passionate talk about Irish solidarity and the importance of a free Palestine, and one of them told the crowd, "We’d like to thank Ed Sheeran for organizing this concert."

During his set, Macklemore said that his entire campaign started with "two words" — free Palestine — and that "those two words are so threatening to some people. They would rather silence those two words than confront what they actually mean. Because freedom that requires another person’s oppression is not freedom at all." He performed all his big hits, as well as his recent protest songs.

The remaining London and Paris dates on the Free Palestine tour are sold out, too. The Paris show goes down 10/29 at Accor Arena.

entry.title: Neil Young Sues Trump PAC Over “Rockin’ In The Free World”
entry.summary: Donald Trump just won’t stop using the Neil Young song “Rockin’ In The Free World” as entrance music at his rallies. As you might imagine, Young is not thrilled about this. Time and again, Young has made his disgust for Trump clear in protest songs and open letters. In 2020, Young sued Trump for his…
entry.content:
Donald Trump just won't stop using the Neil Young song "Rockin' In The Free World" as entrance music at his rallies. As you might imagine, Young is not thrilled about this. Time and again, Young has made his disgust for Trump clear in protest songs and open letters. In 2020, Young sued Trump for his use of the song, and that suit was settled out of court. Now, Young is suing Trump again, claiming that Trump has violated the settlement by continuing to use the song.

As Rolling Stone reports, lawyers for Neil Young have filed a $10 million copyright infringement lawsuit against Donald Trump's political action committee Trump 47 Committee Inc. in Virginia, where the PAC is based. The lawsuit doesn't personally name Trump himself as a defendant.

In their five-page filing, Young's lawyers write that the song "is the opposite of everything that Donald J. Trump stands for" and that Trump was "personally aware that a license would be required" for the song's usage. Young's lawyers claim taht Trump entered to "Rockin' In The Free World" at a midterm rally in Youngstown, Ohio Oct. 12.
